applies_why: The judge counts verses (Matthew 1:18, 25; Luke 1:34) as witnesses pressed against a link without quoting any earlier-round sentence that pressed them or naming a round.
quote: [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union
rule_words: a verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.
room: whether the rule covers verses the judge itself presses against a link: reading one, any verse used against a link needs a named earlier-round quote; reading two, the rule only governs verses counted as unanswered witnesses from a 'cited in' line.
why: The judge lets cited verses count against the C3 link while naming no round and quoting no earlier-round pressing sentence, leaving undone what the rule requires for verses to count.
